items.title: Tracking issue: package without source distribution gets an "incomplete" resolution
items.reason: Canonical tracking issue for universal resolution accepting a wheel-only release that covers some environments, then sync failing with the same missing-distribution error elsewhere. This report adds Windows CPython 3.13 GIL/free-threaded coverage, which the current environment markers cannot distinguish.

items.title: `uv add onnxruntime` fails to fetch latest version of package compatible with my environment's Python
items.reason: Closely related Python compatibility case: universal resolution selects a wheel-only release that cannot install on the requested interpreter instead of backtracking. Maintainers recommend a python_version required environment there; that workaround cannot distinguish 3.13 from 3.13t in this report.

items.title: Backtrack to non-local versions when wheels are missing platform support
items.reason: Partial fix referenced by astral-sh/uv#9711, merged on 2024-12-20. It only considers replacing local versions such as +cpu with their non-local base version when platform wheels are missing. It does not cover ordinary Pympler/pywin32 versions or free-threaded ABI coverage, so it does not establish a regression.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs using authenticated gh. Literal searches covered Pympler, pywin32, pywin32==312, 3.13t, cp313t, required-environments, and the exact missing-source-or-wheel error. Separate conceptual searches covered free-threaded/free-threading/free threading, GIL/no-GIL, markers, universal locking, incomplete resolution, wheel-only dependencies, ABI coverage, and backtracking. Inspected candidate bodies and comments and followed astral-sh/uv#9711 to closed unmerged astral-sh/uv#9928 and merged astral-sh/uv#10046. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#19508 as a mid-upload wheel snapshot problem; astral-sh/uv#14040 and merged astral-sh/uv#14041 as a Windows architecture-marker fix; astral-sh/uv#16434 as interpreter discovery; and astral-sh/uv#2429 as incorrect installation of incompatible ABI wheels. Also inspected astral-sh/uv#12721, astral-sh/uv#11855, and marker/support discussions. Some auxiliary REST searches were rate-limited. Checked repository marker/tag handling and public PyPI release metadata; did not execute the reproduction.

type_reason: The lock-to-sync correctness failure is the incomplete universal-resolution problem already tracked by open astral-sh/uv#9711. Public metadata confirms that Pympler 1.1 adds a Windows-only pywin32 dependency and pywin32 312 has no source distribution or 3.13t wheel; the checkout's marker model cannot express the GIL/free-threaded distinction. The more specific trigger can be centralized in that tracking issue. No evidence shows that a previous fix covered this case and regressed.
summary: astral-sh/uv#9711 is the canonical discussion. astral-sh/uv#9425 covers a similar interpreter-specific wheel gap; merged astral-sh/uv#10046 fixed only a narrower local-version/platform case.
draft_response: This is another instance of the incomplete universal-resolution problem tracked in astral-sh/uv#9711. Pympler 1.1 requires pywin32 on Windows, and pywin32 312 publishes neither a source distribution nor a Python 3.13t wheel. The current environment markers cannot distinguish GIL and free-threaded CPython, so required-environments cannot express that additional requirement. Please continue the discussion in astral-sh/uv#9711 with this reproduction. For now, your pympler==1.0.1 pin avoids that Windows pywin32 dependency.
